newsitem.title: USA: Chicago Fed's Moskow lauds Midwest economic gains.
newsitem.headline: Chicago Fed's Moskow lauds Midwest economic gains.

text.p: Chicago Federal Reserve Bank President Michael Moskow lauded an economic turnaround in the Midwest on Friday in a speech at the University of Missori-St. Louis.

"One thing that's very clear is the Midwest's transformation from over-the-hill to the king of the hill ... from rustbelt to robust," said Moskow. "The old image of a gutted-out region overflowing with obsolete manufacturing plants is a thing of the past."
Moskow said he believed the key to the Midwest's success is that the region's industries have changed how they conduct their businesses.
"The region has changed the way it does business -- its organization, and use of technology," he said.

He added that a study by the Chicago Fed had concluded that the Midwest's success was attributable to better products and prices, not because of external factors such as the performance of the dollar.
Moskow said declining energy prices, cuts in defense spending and even a stronger dollar had benefitted the Midwest.
He also touched on the importance of regional input at Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings, saying it helps to "understand the story behind the numbers."

"The Reserve Banks add a regional perspective and a broad range of ideas to the policy process ... Our regional structure not only insulates us from narrow influences, it also helps us obtain a broad range of information and ideas from people living and working throughout the country," he said.
